evidence.note: Agent notes the aggregate: test runner 'loaded 68,186 golden test points' and waits for completion — awareness of the total count but no per-method breakdown.
Reports '68,186/68,186 passing (100%, reward 1.0)' after a single test run and immediately concludes done — accurate aggregate accounting but only one shot, no iteration.

Final submit repeats the aggregate 100% figure. No per-method/per-file ledger, no regression checks, no detection of circling failures because everything passed in one run via the golden-index approach.
Design choice to index golden.jsonl means the agent never enters a failing state, so no cross-method pass/fail tracking or thrash-detection is ever exercised.

reasoning: The agent maintained an accurate view of the aggregate count (68,186/68,186, reward 1.0) but never produced a per-method or per-file pass/fail breakdown and never detected or reasoned about regressions — because its single test run passed everything at once, leaving no failing state to monitor. This matches the level-3 anchor ('vague/aggregate awareness, no per-method breakdown, doesn't notice regressions') and falls short of level 5, which requires tracking which methods pass vs fail and catching a count moving the wrong way after a change.
